h1: Hydraulic press brakes — CNC, hybrid and NC, 33 to 1,323 US tons
intro: A hydraulic press brake bends sheet and plate between a punch and a V-die with two hydraulic cylinders, giving full force over the whole stroke at the lowest price per ton — the machine for plate, long parts and production. NovoTech sells three kinds in Canada, all on this page: CNC hydraulic press brakes with linear scales, servo valves, crowning and a graphic control — the premium Dener XL in 18 models from 66 to 661 US tons and 5 to 20 ft, and NovoTech's own value line from 55 to 331 tons, heavy-duty and tandem to 1,323 tons and 26 ft; the XH hybrid, an XL with a servo-driven pump that cuts energy by 42 – 58 %; and NC torsion-bar press brakes from 33 to 441 tons for repeat parts in one material. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel and a 1-year warranty, and is installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. For a brake with no hydraulic oil see the electric press brakes; for 33 – 66 ton machines over 4 – 7 ft, the compact press brakes.

faq.q: CNC, hybrid or NC — which hydraulic press brake do I need?
faq.a: A CNC brake measures the ram on linear scales and corrects it through servo valves, calculates the bend from the drawing, crowns the bed and changes material in the program — the machine for mixed work, tight angles and multi-bend parts, and the one most Canadian shops buy. The hybrid is a CNC brake with a servo pump: it costs a little more and pays it back in power, speed and noise when the brake runs all day. An NC brake positions the back gauge and the ram depth from a stored program with the cylinders kept in step by a torsion bar — rigid, cheap to maintain, right for the same parts in one material every day. For 4 – 7 ft work in sheet up to 8 ga, where a 100-ton machine is more than you need, see the compact press brakes.

The premium Dener XL and XH are built in Turkey on the heaviest frame, with ESA or Delem controls, back gauges to 6 axes, sheet followers, robot cells and Dener Canada parts in Mississauga, ON, Canada — the machines for plate, 3/8″ and 1/2″ over 10 to 20 ft, two shifts, a long options list. NovoTech's value line is the same architecture — monoblock frame, Hawe servo valves, linear scales, Delem control — built in China to our specification at about two-thirds of the price: the right buy for a job shop that needs a 100 – 300 ton CNC brake or an NC brake for repeat parts, and the only line that goes to 1,323 tons and 26 ft. Both are installed and supported by the same NovoTech technicians.

faq.q: How much tonnage and length do I need?
faq.a: Air bending mild steel takes about 575 × t² ÷ V US tons per foot, with the thickness t and the V opening in inches: in the standard V = 8 × thickness die that is about 4 tons per foot for 16 ga, 9 for 1/8″, 13.5 for 3/16″, 18 for 1/4″ and 36 for 1/2″ (29 in a 10 × t die); stainless needs about 50 % more, aluminum about half. Add a foot of length to the longest part you bend and about 20 % headroom. A 10 ft × 1/4″ shop is a 175 – 220 ton machine; 10 ft × 3/8″ a 250 – 320 ton machine; 13 ft × 1/2″, bent in a 5 – 6″ V, a 400 – 450 ton machine. Tell us your thickest and longest bend and we size the brake and the tooling.

faq.q: What is a hybrid press brake?
faq.a: On a conventional hydraulic brake the motor and pump run at full speed all day, whether the ram moves or not. The XH hybrid replaces the AC motor and fixed pump with a servo motor driving an inverter pump: the pump turns only while the ram moves, at the speed the ram needs. Dener measures 42 – 58 % energy saving and 17 – 75 % faster approach and return against the XL of the same tonnage, with less heat in the oil and a quieter shop. Everything else — frame, cylinders, valves, tooling, controls — is the XL.

faq.q: Which control comes with the machine?
faq.a: The premium XL comes with the 15″ ESA S640 2D graphic control (Delem DA-66S / 69S and the ESA S875 W 3D control are options): draw the profile, the control calculates the bend sequence, tonnage, back-gauge positions and crowning. The value-line CNC brakes come with Delem DA-53T or DA-58T and the heavy-duty machines with DA-66T; the NC brakes with an Estun E21. All program in inches or millimetres.

faq.q: What back gauge and axes are available?
faq.a: Every CNC machine has the Y1 and Y2 ram axes and an X back-gauge axis on a ball screw and linear guides. Options go up to the 6-axis gauge with X1, X2, R1, R2, Z1 and Z2 — two independently positioned fingers for angled flanges — plus a CNC crowning axis; the NC brakes have X and the depth stop. The back gauge is set by the control for every bend of the program.

faq.q: What tooling fits, and do you stock it?
faq.a: The premium Dener and ISITAN brakes come with European-style (Promecam / Amada) quick-release clamping, and a sectioned punch set with a 2-V die ships with every machine of both lines; the value-line brakes use their own clamping, so tell us which tooling standard your shop already has and we fit the clamps to match. NovoTech stocks Eurostamp press brake tooling in Canada — punches, dies, radius, hemming and joggle tools, gooseneck and special profiles — and sizes it to your machine; Wila hydraulic clamping and American-style adapters are options.

faq.q: What about safety and the Ontario pre-start review?
faq.a: Side guards, an enclosed rear guard, interlocked doors and an anti-panic foot pedal with emergency stop are standard; DSP or Fiessler laser finger protection and light curtains are options we recommend for every CNC machine. In Ontario a new press brake needs a pre-start health and safety review (PSR) under Regulation 851 before it runs; NovoTech prepares the documentation for it.

faq.q: Do you deliver, install and service in Canada?
faq.a: Yes — every press brake is shipped to Mississauga, ON, Canada, unloaded, levelled, commissioned and the operators trained by NovoTech; Dener Canada and NovoTech stock the parts here. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, 600 V standard (208 / 240 / 480 V on request), a 1-year warranty and remote diagnostics through the control.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
